clue.text: Overrates it as a medicine

indicators.note: 'as' asks the solver to recast the preceding letters in a new form, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone exaggerates the benefits of a particular remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overrates it' seems a complaint about the medicine, but its eleven letters, rearranged, spell the answer; 'as' is the weak signal for the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A restorative is a tonic or drug that brings back health and strength.

clue.text: Some under assault for long periods

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A place or army has been under attack for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Eras are long spans of history, so 'for eras' means for ages.

clue.text: Cheated at pontoon?

definitions.meaning: in the card game pontoon a player asking for another card face up says 'twist', so having done so they have this

explanation.walkthrough: Pontoon is the British name for the card game blackjack, where taking another card is called twisting; 'twisted' also means cheated or crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Crooked dealing leaves a victim double-crossed, and in pontoon taking an extra card is the move a player names with this verb.

clue.text: Paradoxical criterion of stability

parts.note: the word means both to sway to and fro and a byword for steadiness, as in 'steady as a ...', hence the paradox

explanation.definitionFit: Stone is the standard image of firmness, yet the same verb means to wobble back and forth.

clue.text: Given medical care at another's expense?

definitions.meaning: a patient seen to by a doctor has been attended to
someone whose meal or drink was paid for by a friend has been stood it

explanation.definitionFit: A doctor attends to a patient, and a host who pays for a friend's dinner stands them it: both senses share the one past participle.

clue.text: Where one may keep the garden spray

definitions.text: Where one may keep the garden spray

parts.words: Where one may keep the garden spray
parts.note: the 'spray' is not a hose or insecticide but a cut bunch of flowers from the garden, kept in an ornamental container of water

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spray' suggests a hosepipe or pesticide stored in a shed; it is a spray of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A vase is the ornamental jar used to hold cut flowers.

clue.text: Moved entrance point to front door

definitions.text: Moved entrance point to front door

parts.words: Moved entrance point to front door
parts.note: the clue pretends to describe shifting a doorway, but 'moved' and 'entrance' both carry the sense of being carried away with delight, and a port is a point of entry

explanation.definitionFit: Someone carried away emotionally, or something carried from one place to another, has been conveyed or enraptured.

clue.text: Unwelcome extra duty

parts.note: 'duty' reads as an additional chore, but it is a levy charged by the government, and a rise in it is unwelcome

explanation.definitionFit: A duty is a tax, so an extra one is a rise in what the Treasury takes.

clue.text: Full marks for bringing an innings to an end?

definitions.meaning: a perfect score on a test marked out of a round number

definitions.text: bringing an innings to an end?
definitions.meaning: in cricket an innings ends when all of a side's batsmen but one are dismissed, i.e. every one of the possible dismissals has happened

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a team's innings is over when ten of its eleven batters are out, so all ten possible dismissals have been taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A flawless score is a perfect mark, and in cricket every possible dismissal taken closes a batting side's turn.

clue.text: One may be powerless without it

definitions.text: One may be powerless without it

parts.words: One may be powerless without it
parts.note: 'powerless' reads as helpless or weak, but literally means having no current supplied to the house

explanation.definitionFit: A power cut leaves a home without mains current, the supply from the grid.

clue.text: Model butterfly?

parts.note: a woman posing for an artist's portrait could be described as having been put on canvas, and the phrase is also the name of a common orange-and-black butterfly

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a common migrant butterfly species and could also describe a woman depicted in oils.

clue.text: Got up, we hear, for breakfast?

indicators.note: signals that the word for 'got up' is only pronounced, not spelt, the same as the answer

parts.note: got up out of bed means rose

explanation.surface: Someone got out of bed in time for breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: Herring roes on toast are a traditional British breakfast dish, which is why the definition carries a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft fish eggs on toast are an old-fashioned morning meal in Britain, so they are breakfast by example.

clue.text: Can recall Napoleon's place of exile

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the word for 'can' is read backwards

parts.note: 'can' means 'is able', giving able

explanation.surface: A question of whether Napoleon's island exile can be remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb about remembering; it is the synonym to be reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon was banished to this Mediterranean island off Tuscany in 1814 before his escape.

clue.text: Old ones like this have little sense

definitions.text: Old ones like this have little sense

indicators.note: letters that make little sense as they stand need rearranging into a word that does

explanation.surface: Old people of a certain kind are said to be rather foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'Old ones' are rearranged; 'have little sense' is both the signal and, with the rest, the description of the fools the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: A noodle is an old slang word for a simpleton, so noodles are people lacking wit.

clue.text: Joins with the edges

definitions.meaning: to take someone's part, as in 'he always ... with his brother', is to join them
the borders or flanks of anything

explanation.surface: Something is fastened together along its borders.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb is used with 'with': to side with someone is to join their camp, so 'with' is the link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a team's part is aligning with it, and the flanks or margins of a shape are its boundaries.

clue.text: A central American team is able to kick off with me

indicators.note: kicking off means starting, so the word 'me' goes at the front of the rest

parts.note: taken as written
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a cricket or football team
'is able' means can

explanation.surface: A footballer from Central America gets the team going, kicking off alongside the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kick off' suggests football, which XI (eleven, a side) supports; here it just means 'start with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mexico lies in Central America, so a citizen of it is a Central American native.

clue.text: Measure is about the right length

indicators.note: the word for 'measure' goes around the abbreviation for right

parts.note: to mete is to measure or deal out, as in 'mete out punishment'
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A measurement is roughly the correct length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Measure' wants to be the definition, but it is METE, which goes about R; the answer, a length, comes from the end of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A metre is a unit of distance of a hundred centimetres.

clue.text: Like the cubed root of carrot, perhaps

definitions.text: Like the cubed root of carrot, perhaps

parts.words: Like the cubed root of carrot, perhaps
parts.note: 'cubed root' borrows maths language, but means a carrot, a root vegetable, chopped into small cubes

explanation.definitionFit: Vegetables chopped into small cubes in the kitchen are said to be cut this way.

clue.text: The head cook may make it

definitions.meaning: an old word for the crown of the head, often a bald one
a cook might prepare a smooth meat or fish paste, usually written with an accent

explanation.surface: A head chef might be the one to prepare it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The head cook' reads as one phrase, a chef in charge; split it after 'head'.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown of the skull is an old term for the head, and a savoury spread of liver is the dish a cook makes.

clue.text: Bare sort of hill in Scotland

indicators.note: a sort of the word 'bare' is a rearranged version of it

explanation.surface: A bleak, treeless kind of Scottish hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots a brae is a steep slope or hillside.

clue.text: They are kept in a box in the car

definitions.text: They are kept in a box in the car

parts.words: They are kept in a box in the car
parts.note: the 'box' is not a glovebox for maps but the housing for the toothed wheels that change a car's speed

explanation.definitionFit: A car's gearbox contains the toothed wheels that the driver shifts between.

clue.text: Stone jar with nickel lining

indicators.note: the chemical symbol lines the inside of the word for 'jar', sitting within it

parts.note: to jar is to grate, as on the nerves
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel

explanation.surface: A stone storage jar has a nickel lining inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jar' reads as a container; it is the verb, to grate.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite is a hard igneous rock used for building and worktops.

clue.text: Stud's list put on board

indicators.note: being put on a vessel means going aboard, inside it, so the word for list is placed within the ship

parts.note: on board a ship: SS, short for steamship, stands for the vessel
a table is a list or chart of figures

explanation.surface: A breeding stallion's details are put up on a noticeboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is a crossword convention for inside SS, a steamship. A stud is a horse-breeding establishment, the same thing as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud farm keeps horses housed in buildings, so a stud is a set of horse buildings and their stock.

clue.text: They are inclined to support overhead development

definitions.text: They are inclined to support overhead development

parts.words: They are inclined to support overhead development
parts.note: 'inclined to support' reads as willing to back a project, but means sloping beams that hold up a roof

explanation.definitionFit: Sloping timbers that carry a pitched roof are the beams of its frame.

clue.text: Moral code followed by a student

indicators.note: the pieces after it come after the word for code

parts.note: an ethic is a moral code or principle
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A rule of conduct is observed by a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moral code' reads as one phrase; split it, with 'Moral' the definition and 'code' giving ETHIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ethical means behaving in a principled, upright way.

clue.text: Still on level terms

definitions.meaning: used for emphasis, as in 'better still'

explanation.surface: Two sides remain equal in the contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed before a comparative it adds emphasis, as 'yet' does, and two scores that are square are balanced.

clue.text: Scotsman upset about unknown fascist

indicators.note: the turned name goes around the letter for an unknown
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name
z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: A Scot is angry about a mystery right-winger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns IAN to NAI, and 'about' puts it round Z.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of Hitler's party is the archetypal far-right extremist.

clue.text: An outside number that's not designated

indicators.note: the word 'an' sits outside the abbreviation for number, wrapping it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rank outsider in a race is unnamed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: an author or work that is unnamed is anonymous.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for anonymous, it marks a poem or quotation whose author is unnamed.

clue.text: Word associated with poker — it's not flush

definitions.meaning: a variety of the card game with some cards dealt face up
a knob or rivet head that stands proud of a surface rather than level with it

explanation.surface: A poker term is mentioned, and the player's hand is not a flush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flush' is a poker hand, but here means level with a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven-card ___ is a poker variant, and a raised nailhead projects instead of lying level.

clue.text: A spot of trouble over a pupil?

definitions.text: A spot of trouble over a pupil?

parts.words: A spot of trouble over a pupil?
parts.note: the 'pupil' is not a schoolchild in difficulty but the dark centre of the eye, and the 'spot' is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid above it

explanation.definitionFit: An infected swelling on the eyelid sits just above the eye's dark centre.

clue.text: Tony Italian? Could be English

indicators.note: suggests the name's letters could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Is Tony Italian? He might be English.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of TONY ITALIAN are rearranged; 'English' defines by example, which the question mark and 'Could be' acknowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Being English is one example of a citizenship or national identity.

clue.text: Children may be found playing it

definitions.text: Children may be found playing it

parts.words: Children may be found playing it
parts.note: in the game, the players conceal themselves and are found, so being found is part of the play

explanation.definitionFit: Children hide while one of them counts, then searches for the rest: a classic playground game.
